title: Washington AI Laws

reading.body:
Washington's only AI-specific law regulates companion chatbots, not the data centers or power that scale AI.

The law, HB2225, passed on 2026-03-24 and targets the consumer-facing end of AI. It requires operators to disclose that a chatbot is artificial and not human, with recurring notifications. It adds protections for minors, restricts sexually explicit content and manipulative engagement techniques, and requires operators to maintain and publicly disclose protocols for detecting suicidal ideation or self-harm.

This is a narrow slice of AI policy. It governs how a chatbot talks to a person, not how models are trained, where compute is sited, or how much power that compute draws. A state can pass a chatbot disclosure rule without touching the grid, the substations, or the interconnection queue that determine whether AI capacity gets built.

The data covers one law and nothing else. It does not show pending bills, failed bills, or regulations that are not statutes. It does not say how many operators fall under the law, what penalties attach, or whether any enforcement has occurred. One law is not a trend, and this page cannot tell you whether Washington will regulate compute or power next.

Enacted AI laws in Washington

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • HB2225: Revised for 1st substitute: Regulating artificial intelligence companion chatbots. passed 2026-03-24

    The act regulates AI companion chatbots by requiring operators to disclose that the chatbot is artificial and not human, with recurring notifications. It imposes additional protections for minors, including restrictions on sexually explicit content and manipulative engagement techniques. It also requires operators to maintain protocols for detecting and responding to suicidal ideation or self-harm and to publicly disclose those protocols.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Washington. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
